title: Discovery: Elysian Data - Migration from OpenAI to Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery focused on migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Customer is cost-sensitive and has mixed infra (some vLLM/TGI runs on prem). Main concerns: eval parity, latency, data residency/VPC, KMS, and rollout plan. SE offered benchmarking, pilot/DC sizing, and security docs. Agreed next steps: share Dedicated pricing, security pack, and run eval parity test on sample prompts.
next_steps: Samir to send Dedicated pricing and capacity options (include burst tiers)
Lina to share eval parity test template and runbook + propose timeline
Customer to provide sample prompt set and 2 weeks of traffic profile
Schedule pilot kickoff after pricing agreement
action_items: Samir Patel: send Dedicated pricing + example SLOs (due 2026-11-19)
Lina Gomez: share eval parity harness + instructions for model/seeded prompts (due 2026-11-20)
Aisha Khan: upload sample prompts and traffic profile to shared drive (due 2026-11-22)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Aisha (Elysian - Head ML), Marcus (Infra Eng), Priya (CTO)
Shared docs: https://redwood.enterprise/deck (AE deck), Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/elysian/prompt-set (customer samples)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh quick intros? I'm Samir, AE on the enterprise team, with Lina our SE.
[00:12] Aisha: hi all, I'm Aisha, lead ML at Elysian, we run customer-facing summarization and extraction pipelines, currently on OpenAI and some self-hosted vLLM for high-volume internal jobs.
[00:25] Marcus: Marcus here, infra, we own our K8s clusters and some TGI instances, looking at options to reduce cost and get tighter data controls.
[00:33] Priya: Priya, CTO, i'm mostly here for security and sketched timeline — curious about SLA and migration effort.

[02:05] Lina: great, thanks. quick agenda - understand current stack, pain points, compatibility questions (vLLM/TGI), security/ops needs, and propose next steps. does that align?
[02:22] Aisha: yep, sounds good. high level — we send ~30M tokens/day to OpenAI, big spike weekdays, and have 3 internal heavy-batch jobs on vLLM. costs have ballooned, and we need more predictable pricing and data residency.

[04:10] Samir: got it. when you say vLLM runs, those are on-prem GPU clusters? are you using vLLM as the runtime and TGI for some endpoints?
[04:27] Marcus: yeah, vLLM for low-latency KV fast-line inference, TGI for some legacy endpoints where we need custom sampling. to be honest we have differences in behavior between OpenAI models and our local stacks — prompt tuning everywhere.

[06:00] Lina: a few things we usually cover for migrations: model compatibility and eval parity — we can run an eval harness against your prompt set to show token-level parity vs your baseline; throughput and latency SLOs — Redwood Dedicated supports pinned GPU pools and autoscaling; security — VPC/private control plane, KMS/HSM, SOC2 plus audit logs.
[06:30] Priya: how close is the output to OpenAI? we need parity on our NLU metrics or this will be hard to flip.

[07:05] Samir: absolutely. we typically do an eval parity run (we call it a parity test) — we take your sample prompts, run them through the candidate model on Dedicated and compare F1/ROUGE/utility metrics to your OpenAI baseline. in many cases it's within noise, sometimes we recommend fine-tuning or prompt changes.
[07:30] Aisha: are you saying Redwood runs your own models or we can bring our weights? we have some custom fine-tuned checkpoints.

[07:55] Lina: two paths — hosted models from our catalog (we've onboarded open models with curated performance profiles), or Dedicated/private where you can deploy your own weights behind the same API. Dedicated supports commonly used runtimes including vLLM and TGI-compatible execution paths; runtime naming sometimes mismatches in docs so we can show concrete configs.

[09:20] Marcus: important: we need the ability to keep keys in our KMS, and traffic inside our VPC, and strict audit logging. do you support customer-managed KMS?
[09:36] Samir: yes — for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations, and Dedicated can be placed in a VPC with a private control plane. audit logs and token-level traces are available in the Console.

[11:00] Aisha: okay latency — our SLAs need p50 under 200ms for small context endpoints, p95 under 700ms. can Dedicated handle that with your batching?
[11:18] Lina: for short-context generative calls, Dedicated with GPU pools and prefix caching can achieve those SLOs depending on model size and instance type. there is a tradeoff: batching improves cost but increases tail latency. we can recommend kernel choices and quantization profiles to meet your latency targets.

[13:40] Marcus: we've experimented with quantization on vLLM and saw behavior differences in completions — any gotchas?
[13:55] Lina: yes quantization can introduce small distribution shifts — part of our Eval Optimize flow is to recommend quantization profiles per workload and run the parity tests post-quant to measure regressions. we keep a "regression alert" tied to your prompt set.

[16:05] Priya: what about failover — if Dedicated pool is saturated or an upgrade goes bad, what's the fallback?
[16:18] Samir: smart routing — we can set policies to fallback to a compatible model or to Hosted API depending on your policy; rollouts support canary/A-B with automatic rollback on regressions.

[18:50] Aisha: our team uses a lot of prompt engineering and we rely on the exact newline and tokenization behavior — does Redwood preserve tokenization parity with OpenAI?
[19:05] Lina: tokenization differences exist across tokenizers. in parity runs we perform tokenized comparisons and can recommend small prompt adaptions. where critical, we can run the same tokenizer pipeline inside Dedicated to reduce drift.

[21:40] Marcus: talk to me about throughput — we have peaks up to 700 RPS on short calls, and batch jobs that need sustained throughput for 10 minutes. how do you size Dedicated?
[21:56] Samir: we size by expected concurrent streams and average sequence length. for bursty workloads we recommend a reserved base pool plus burst capacity; autoscaling policies can add capacity quickly but you should define acceptable cold-start behavior. we'll propose a sizing estimate after we see the 2-week traffic profile.

[24:10] Aisha: on compliance — SOC2 is necessary, do you provide SOC2 + ISO certifications and the compliance pack?
[24:23] Samir: yes, we are SOC2 Type II and have ISO attestation. I'll share the security pack and SOC2 report under NDA. also SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported in the Console.

[26:40] Priya: any challenges with running open-source models we care about? we've seen differences when running llama-derivative weights on vLLM vs TGI.
[26:55] Lina: runtime differences exist — vLLM's KV cache behavior and some sampling kernels differ. Redwood's runtime does kernel selection and has been tuned for typical Llama variants; we'll surface config diffs and reproducibility notes in the parity report. sometimes small tweak in temperature/sampling helps reproduce OpenAI-like outputs.

[29:10] Marcus: network setup: do we manage the nodes in our account or do you? we have a restrictive security posture.
[29:22] Samir: Dedicated can be deployed in your cloud account (private control plane) or as a managed Dedicated with VPC peering. for very strict setups we do Private deployment in customer VPC or on-prem. either way you control KMS and network egress rules.

[31:40] Aisha: pricing — show me the economics vs OpenAI, we need a ballpark for 30M tokens/day and the heavy batch jobs.
[31:55] Samir: i'll send a cost model — it includes reserved capacity monthly plus usage and a per-token estimate factoring caching and batching. early estimate is often 30-50% lower than public API at scale but depends on your model selection and cache hit rates.

[34:05] Priya: if we bring our weights, what is the onboarding time?
[34:17] Lina: from deployment to pilot usually 2-4 weeks: parity runs (1 week), pilot sizing and validation (1-2 weeks), and then cutover planning. we can compress that if you provide prompts and traffic earlier.

[36:00] Aisha: who will be our contacts for the pilot?
[36:07] Samir: we'll be the point people — Samir for commercial, Lina as SE lead. we'll loop in an account engineer for the Dedicated sizing.

[37:40] Marcus: small nit — do you support our existing observability stack? Grafana/Prometheus traces?
[37:50] Lina: yes we emit metrics and traces, and you can pull via our tracing hooks; we also provide token-level cost breakdowns in the Console.

[39:10] Priya: any blockers you foresee?
[39:16] Lina: only if there are proprietary kernel dependencies in your custom weights that prevent running on our runtime; otherwise most blockers are operational and mitigated with pilot.

[40:00] Samir: ok quick recap — we'll share Dedicated pricing + sizing estimate, Lina will share the eval parity harness and runbook, Aisha will provide sample prompts & 2 weeks traffic, we'll aim to kick off parity tests next week.
[40:20] Aisha: sounds good, appreciate the thoroughness.
[40:30] Priya: thanks everyone, we'll aim to have sample data by Monday.
[40:40] Samir: great, I'll send notes and links after the call. thanks all.

End of transcript. some transcription artifacts: occasional speaker swaps and mis-typed product names (Redwood Dediated / KV cash) noted in internal notes.
